summary: Jeanne Bliss argues that sustainable growth comes from building a 'beloved' company that serves the lives of customers and employees, not a company that reflexively competes with others. The talk centers on five deliberate decisions—believing in customers, clarifying purpose, being present, being real, and creating lasting memories—that together cultivate trust, loyalty, and higher margins. Through real-world examples (Trader Joe’s memory-driven service, IKEA’s price-first design grounded in customers’ life, USAA’s life-centered onboarding, Southwest’s proactive fault recovery, Lands’ End anecdotes, IHOP hiring for values), Bliss illustrates how operational reliability and humane apologies reinforce an emotional bond. She emphasizes memory creation as the currency of a brand, hiring for memory creators, and the power of proactive rescue (love notes, “chief forgiveness officer”) to turn service failures into growth opportunities. The transcript provides a practical framework—the four-part peace process for recovery—and challenges leaders to ensure customers tell the story they want, and employees embody the same life-centered values in every interaction.
title: Earning Your Customer's Rave: A Life-Centered Framework for Beloved Companies (Jeanne Bliss keynote)
